slides.title: Why does she go from hugs to bites?
slides.text: Spoiler: it's not her personality and it's not you. It's hormones. They change every day, and so does she.

slides.title: Estrogen, the Energizer
slides.text: Brings energy and good mood. She wants to talk, flirt and make plans.
slides.analogy: The friend who texts "let's go out!" on a Friday night

slides.title: Progesterone, the couch cat
slides.text: Calms and slows things down. Sleepy, hungry, blanket-seeking.
slides.analogy: The couch after Thanksgiving dinner: full, warm, zero desire to move

slides.title: Testosterone, the surprise guest
slides.text: Yes, she has it too. Not much, but it brings drive, confidence and desire. It spikes mid-cycle.
slides.analogy: The locker room before a big game

slides.title: FSH and LH, the brain's foremen
slides.text: They sit in the head and give orders. FSH: "Grow an egg!" LH: "Ready, release!"
slides.analogy: The coach yelling "go-go-go!" from the sideline

slides.title: The cycle map
slides.text: A cycle is usually about 28 days, but anywhere from 21 to 35 is normal. Four phases: period, follicular, ovulation and luteal, with PMS at the end of the luteal phase. Borders shift by a couple of days.

slides.title: Period
slides.text: The uterus resets: the old lining comes out. Cramps, belly and back pain, low energy.
slides.analogy: Getting tackled by the whole defensive line. Then they run the play again

slides.title: Follicular phase
slides.text: Estrogen rises, and so do energy and mood. Her mind is sharp.
slides.analogy: Friday afternoon, great sleep, payday, sunshine

slides.title: Ovulation
slides.text: LH gives the signal and the egg is released. Peak energy, confidence and wanting to be noticed.

slides.title: Luteal phase
slides.text: Progesterone is in charge now. Calm, sleepy, craving sweets.

slides.title: PMS
slides.text: Hormones crash. Irritable and teary out of nowhere, bloating, sore breasts, craving sweets and wanting everyone to back off.
slides.analogy: Starving, sleep-deprived, stuck in traffic at 2% battery, and someone asks "why so grumpy?"

slides.title: The main things to remember
slides.text: 1. It's not drama, it's chemistry. 2. It runs in a loop: after the storm, the sun comes back. 3. Nothing needs fixing. Most of the time, being there is enough.

slides.title: Hugs work in every phase
slides.text: Thanks for figuring this out. It really means a lot to her.

pages.text: Estrogen climbs to the middle, LH spikes, progesterone rises in the second half. At the end everything drops. The chart uses her own phase lengths.

pages.text: Four episodes of one season. Repeats every month.

items: Belly, back and even legs hurt

pages.title: PMS
pages.text: The egg wasn't needed, and both hormones crash. The body is in mild shock.
items: Irritation and tears out of nowhere
Craves sweets and wants everyone to back off

pages.text: And then someone asks: "Why are you so grumpy?"
pages.todo: Don't argue and don't joke about PMS. Hug her and bring snacks

pages.title: The main things to remember
items: It's chemistry, not whims. She doesn't choose to feel this way.
It goes in circles. After the storm the sun comes back in a couple of weeks.
Nothing needs fixing. Most of the time, just being there is enough.

pages.title: Now you get it
pages.text: I'll tell you every day where she is. Your job is not to get lost.

pages.title: Get to know her
pages.text: Charts are general, she is one of a kind. Send her a short quiz and the tips will be about her.

slides.title: Cravings aren't weakness
slides.text: In the second half of the cycle, many women crave sweets and carbs more. It's a common thing, not a lack of willpower.

slides.title: What's going on inside
slides.text: After ovulation progesterone takes the lead, and right before her period hormones drop fast. The body burns a bit more energy, and the brain asks for quick calories.

slides.title: Sugar and mood
slides.text: Before her period, mood often dips. Chocolate is the fastest pick-me-up around, and the brain remembers that.

slides.title: Your move
slides.text: Don't comment on what or how much she eats. Just bring her favorite, no questions asked.

slides.title: If she wants something lighter
slides.text: Nuts, fruit, a warm cocoa. Offer, don't push: it's her call.

pages.text: Cravings usually grow in the second half of the cycle, when progesterone rules, and peak before her period, when hormones drop.

pages.title: Three things better left unsaid
items: "Sweets again?". Sounds like blame, even if you didn't mean it.
"Isn't that enough?". It's her call, not yours.
PMS jokes. They're not funny. At all.

books.title: How to help when she feels awful

slides.title: Nothing needs fixing
slides.text: When she feels bad, she usually doesn't need a game plan. She needs you around.

slides.title: Ask what she wants
slides.text: "Want a hug or some space?" One simple question takes half the tension away.

slides.title: Listen now, debate later
slides.text: Even if you disagree, now is not the time to win the point. Talk it over when she feels better.

slides.title: Care with your hands
slides.text: Tea, a blanket, a heating pad, dinner she didn't have to make. She'll notice small things more than big words.

slides.title: And afterwards
slides.text: When it passes, don't bring that day up again. Just be there on good days and bad ones.

pages.title: Better not to
items: Don't downplay it. "Come on, it can't hurt that much" doesn't help.
Don't joke about PMS. Even if you really want to.
Don't disappear. Quietly being there beats "call me if you need anything".

pages.title: When it's over
pages.text: Don't bring that day up again. No "you really lost it back then".
